## Rationale

Ki-67 (encoded by *MKI67*) is the canonical proliferation marker because it is expressed in all active phases of the cell cycle (G1, S, G2, M) but absent in G0 quiescence, and its abundance rises progressively through the cycle — so single-cell Ki-67 protein levels are a quasi-quantitative readout of proliferative state (Gerdes et al., *J Immunol* 1984; Scholzen & Gerdes, *J Cell Physiol* 2000). Ki-67 is also a validated prognostic/predictive breast cancer marker (Yerushalmi et al., *Lancet Oncol* 2010; Dowsett et al., *JNCI* 2011). Variation in Ki-67 protein among tumor cells should therefore map onto variation in **cell-cycle state**, and the key question is which molecular program gates cell-cycle entry in breast cancer.

In breast cancer, the best-established gatekeeper is estrogen receptor α (ESR1). Double-labeling studies showed that ER-positive cells in the normal breast and in ER+ tumors are rarely Ki-67-positive — proliferation is concentrated in the ER-negative/low tumor-cell compartment (Clarke et al., *JNCI* 1997; Shoker et al., *Eur J Cancer* 1999). Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic atlases confirmed this at genome scale: in ER+ tumors, cycling (*MKI67*/*TOP2A*-high) tumor cells are predominantly ESR1-low (Karaayvaz et al., *Nat Commun* 2018; Wu et al., *Nat Genet* 2021; Bassez et al., *Cell* 2021). Mechanistically, this reflects antagonism between two transcriptional programs: the **ER–FOXA1–GATA3 luminal differentiation program** (*ESR1, PGR, TFF1, XBP1, AGR2*), which in situ is associated with a non-proliferative state, and the **MYC–E2F–cyclin D/CDK4/6–RB axis**, whose activation drives G1/S entry and transcription of proliferation genes including *MKI67* (Bretones et al., *BBA* 2015; Chen et al., *Nat Rev Cancer* 2009). Consistent with this, CDK4/6 inhibition preferentially arrests luminal ER+ breast cancer models and suppresses Ki-67 (Finn et al., *Breast Cancer Res* 2009).

CosMx spatial molecular imaging measures RNA and protein in the same, spatially registered FFPE cells (He et al., *Nat Methods* 2022), making this mechanism directly testable at single-cell resolution: same-cell regression of Ki-67 protein intensity against ER-module and cell-cycle-module transcripts, plus spatial statistics on Ki-67-high cells.

## Hypothesis

**Among tumor-enriched breast cancer cells, Ki-67 protein abundance is determined by cell-cycle state set by antagonism between ERα (ESR1) luminal differentiation signaling and MYC–E2F–CDK4/6 cell-cycle entry: ESR1/PGR/TFF1-high cells are held in G0 and are Ki-67-low, whereas cells that downregulate the ER program and activate MYC/E2F targets (*MKI67, TOP2A, CCNB1, UBE2C, PCNA*) enter cycle and accumulate Ki-67 protein.** Spatially, Ki-67-high cells should occur as focal clusters of ESR1-low cycling cells rather than being randomly distributed.

## Testable predictions

1. **Same-cell RNA–protein concordance:** Ki-67 protein intensity correlates with *MKI67* transcript and a G2M/cell-cycle module score (*MKI67, TOP2A, CCNB1, UBE2C, CENPF, PCNA*) in the same cells.
2. **Inverse ER relationship:** Ki-67 protein intensity anticorrelates with *ESR1* RNA/protein and an ER-target module (*PGR, TFF1, XBP1, AGR2*), strongest in ER+/luminal tumors; the ER module should explain Ki-67 variation beyond *MKI67* RNA alone.
3. **Spatial structure:** Ki-67-high cells cluster non-randomly (Ripley's K / neighbor-enrichment analysis), and those clusters are ESR1-low; if paracrine mitogenic input contributes, Ki-67-high cells will sit closer than chance expectation to ESR1-high tumor cells or CAF-rich stromal niches.
4. **Orthogonal validation:** dual IF/RNAscope for ESR1 and MKI67/Ki-67 in the same FFPE block; functional tests — palbociclib (CDK4/6) or MYC knockdown collapses the Ki-67-high compartment in ER+ patient-derived organoids, while estradiol stimulation expands Ki-67 positivity preferentially in ER-low tumor cells.

## Established vs. novel

This is primarily **(a) established literature knowledge**: the ER–proliferation dissociation (Clarke et al. 1997; Shoker et al. 1999; Wu et al. 2021) and MYC/E2F control of *MKI67* (Bretones et al. 2015; Chen et al. 2009) are well documented. The novel element is the test rather than the mechanism: CosMx uniquely enables same-cell RNA–protein quantification and spatial statistics, and prediction 3 — quantifying focal, ESR1-low proliferative clusters and their neighbor relationships — is, to my knowledge, an untested spatial refinement of the established dissociation.
